title: Catalog fingerprints and synthetic benchmarks for safe version pinning
creator: Nora Patel
description: Add a repeatable process and metadata schema fields to capture a deterministic fingerprint for newly ingested models, plus a small synthetic benchmark suite and conventions for publishing performance profiles. Goal: enable safe, auditable version pinning (hash + perf signature) and publish human- and machine-readable docs that teams can rely on for rollout decisions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Ingest pipeline emits model_fingerprint (sha256) and model_signature (short perf vector) into catalog metadata. 2) Onboarded models have an associated synthetic benchmark result (latency P50, P95; throughput tokens/s; memory usage). 3) Docs updated with pinning workflow and example rollouts. 4) Automated lint fails if fingerprint or perf vector missing for new model publishes. 5) Security review completed and signed off.
tasks: Define fingerprint format and collision mitigations (sha256 + manifest manifestization)
Design minimal synthetic benchmark harness (10 prompts, varying lengths, tokenization spec)
Implement metadata schema changes and backward-compatible ingest path
Add publishable perf profile artifact in S3 and index link in catalog metadata
Update onboarding docs and quickstart with pin examples
Add metadata linter rule and CI check for catalog PRs
Coordinate security review for fingerprint storage and signing

notes_and_tradeoffs: Using sha256 over a canonicalized manifest keeps fingerprints deterministic across rehosting, but requires strict manifest normalization rules.
Synthetic benchmarks are intentionally small to keep onboarding fast; they do not replace full-scale performance sweeps but provide a stable perf signature for regressions.
Storing perf artifacts increases catalog storage costs; we keep 90-day retention by default and offer longer retention behind a flag.
Decision: publish numeric perf-vector (p50,p95,tokens_per_second,memory_mb) plus a short qualitative tag (fast|balanced|memory-heavy).
qa_plan: Add unit tests for manifest canonicalization, e2e test that ingest pipeline writes fingerprint and perf artifact, and a catalog UI smoke test that shows the badge and links. Run bench harness in staging on a dedicated pool and validate results are stable across 3 runs.
deployment_plan: Deploy ingest changes behind feature flag. Start with internal models only, then gate third-party publishes until security review completes. Enable linter rule after 2-week pilot.
risks: Fingerprint collisions if manifest normalization is under-specified
Bench harness can be noisy if not isolated; false regressions possible
Teams may rely too heavily on small synthetic suite — need guidance in docs
